Purpose: Qualification of smaller CSV write buffers; neither experiment is adopted as the general default.

NET10.DifferenceFromInitialHarness: Row-writer optional default resolved in setup instead of embedded at compile time; timed baseline receives the same 262144 value

Policies.Name: 64k

Disposition.Status: Declined as general write default; production patch reversed
Disposition.Reason: Lower allocation is repeatable, but throughput does not qualify a universal default. Native and rotated observations disagree; identical-build controls show instance/host sensitivity. The 25K async plain-file followup remains 1.031/1.088 with means 1.025/1.152; row-writer 25K is 1.019/1.098. Further policy-specific qualification is required before adopting a smaller default.
Disposition.Review: The 16KiB contract review found no actionable defects. The 64KiB policy changes only that constant; no final acceptance review was claimed.

NET10.DifferenceFromInitialHarness: Row-writer optional default resolved in setup instead of embedded at compile time; timed baseline receives the same 262144 value

NET8.DifferenceFromInitialHarness: Row-writer optional default resolved in setup instead of embedded at compile time; timed baseline receives the same 262144 value

Validation: Each experiment passes Windows CSV correctness (655 NET10, 655 NET8, 463 Framework), plus 39 independently field-validated fixture combinations per actual runtime and snapshot build. Native NET8 runs in NET8; all rotations run in NET10. The 16KiB experiment also builds netstandard2.0. No Linux/macOS buffer acceptance qualification is claimed.
Limits: Screening and bounded controls only; full 240-workload timing was not run after these policies failed qualification.
File measurements include create/replace and flush to the operating system, without durable-storage flush.
Busy Windows workstation; retain all outliers and conflicting observations. No portable throughput ranking.
Warmed managed allocated bytes are not retained or peak memory.
An old compiled caller retains the old optional argument; a recompiled caller receives the candidate default. Setup resolves each build default while benchmark IL remains identical.
